citation: Raza et al. 2010, Int. J. Hydrogen Energy 35:2684

materials.synthesis_route: one-step co-precipitation (nitrates + Na2CO3 co-precipitated in same process)
materials.notes: Novel one-step process is the paper's main contribution. Sintering 800 C 2 h. Cell 13 mm diameter, 0.7 cm2 active area, 0.8-1.0 mm total thickness (electrolyte 0.3-0.5 mm; pellet_thickness_um recorded as midpoint 400). Cell then sintered 600 C 0.5 h. Metal ion : carbonate ion molar ratio = 1:2. Sm:Ce ratio not explicitly stated for the one-step (only 1:4 stated for the two-step comparison sample); dopant_fraction left null. No direct conductivity measurement reported (only I-V/I-P fuel cell characteristics). Fuel gas not stated in text.

materials.synthesis_route: two-step: (1) co-precipitation of SDC with NH3 at pH 10, sintered 700 C 2 h; (2) mixed with LiNaCO3 powder, sintered 700 C 30 min
materials.notes: Comparison baseline (not the paper's own novel material). Sm:Ce = 1:4 (20%) explicit. SDC:LiNaCO3 weight ratio not stated. Cell dimensions same as one-step sample (13 mm, 0.7 cm2 active, 0.8-1.0 mm total, 0.3-0.5 mm electrolyte -> midpoint 400 um). Sintered at 600 C 0.5 h after pressing. Pmax ~1000 mW/cm2 at 590 C. No direct conductivity value reported.

extraction_notes: Paper reports fuel cell I-V/I-P performance for two electrolyte compositions but no explicit ionic-conductivity numbers, no activation energies, no atmosphere/fuel spec in the text, no durability hours, no relative density. Pellet electrolyte thickness given as a range 0.3-0.5 mm; recorded as midpoint 400 um in schema. dopant_fraction for the one-step SDC-Na2CO3 not explicitly stated (though 'SDC' conventionally implies 20% Sm) - left null per the no-guessing rule. Two-step comparison sample uses LiNaCO3 secondary phase, different from the paper's headline SDC-Na2CO3 material.
